h: Great Yarmouth tips for clued-up climbers
p: Seaside holidays and climbing sessions don't always fit together neatly, so here's how to make it easy. Book your slot as early as you can once you've seen the weather forecast, because wet days in peak season send every family in town looking for something indoors. Allow a couple of hours for the visit, including check-in, harnesses and the safety briefing.

Every climber needs a participation form, signed by a parent or guardian for under-18s. Fill it in on your phone back at the caravan and you'll sail through the desk. There's usually a minimum age for climbers too, with supervision rules for little ones, so check those when you book.
Climbing straight after a big plate of chips is not the move. Eat light, drink water and leave buckets, spades and sandy flip-flops behind. Trainers and comfy clothes are the order of the day.

When you're done, there's loads more to enjoy. The Time and Tide Museum, in an old herring-curing works, tells the story of the town's fishing past brilliantly. Merrivale Model Village on the seafront is a charming old-school stop, and Sea Life Great Yarmouth is handy if the rain hasn't let up. Fancy a quieter beach? Gorleston, just across the river mouth, has a lovely sweep of sand and a more relaxed feel than the Golden Mile.
